questions.question:
Identify the degree of comparison of the adjective in the following administrative sentence:
"The Supreme Court is the highest appellate authority in the judicial hierarchy."

options.text: Positive Degree
Comparative Degree
Superlative Degree
Definite Degree

questions.explanation: Adjective 'highest' mein inflectional suffix '-est' laga hua hai aur usse pehle definite article 'the' maujood hai. Ye judicial hierarchy ke apex authority ko isolate kar raha hai. Isliye ye clearly Superlative Degree hai. Positive form 'high' hoti hai aur comparative form 'higher' hoti hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Superlative Degree represents the supreme limit of a quality within a group.
questions.hint: Adjective mein '-est' suffix aur pehle 'the' article laga hua hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct comparative and superlative forms of the adjective 'brave'?

options.text: braveer, braveest
braver, bravest
more brave, most brave
bravier, braviest

questions.explanation: Adjective 'brave' single-syllable word hai jo already silent '-e' par end hota hai. Rule ke mutabiq, double 'e' nahi lagaya jata; simply '-r' aur '-st' joda jata hai: brave ➔ braver ➔ bravest. Option (A) double 'e' likhta hai jo spelling error hai. Option (D) 'y' to 'i' rule ko unnecessarily apply kar raha hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Adjectives ending in silent '-e' add only '-r' and '-st'.
questions.hint: Agar word ke end mein pehle se 'e' ho, toh dobara 'e' nahi lagta; sirf 'r' aur 'st' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Identify the grammatically correct sentence free from double comparative redundancy:
"The new judicial guidelines are ___ than the old rules."

options.text: more clearer
clearer
much more clearer
clearest

questions.explanation: Adjective 'clear' monosyllabic hai aur regular comparative suffix '-er' lekar 'clearer' banta hai. Iske aage alag se 'more' lagana redundant double comparative error hai ('*more clearer' is wrong). Option (C) mein bhi redundant 'more' hai. Option (D) 'clearest' superlative hai jabki yahan do sets ('new guidelines' vs 'old rules') compare ho rahe hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Single inflection law — never combine '-er' suffix with 'more'.
questions.hint: 'Clearer' ke sath 'more' lagana redundancy error hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the appropriate comparative form:
"The investigating officer collected ___ evidence than was initially presented in the FIR."

options.text: manier
more
most
much

questions.explanation: Noun 'evidence' uncountable noun hai jiska positive quantifier 'much' hota hai. 'Much' ka comparative form 'more' hota hai (much ➔ more ➔ most). Sentence mein conjunction 'than' hai jo comparative degree demand karta hai. Option (A) '*manier' non-existent word hai. Option (C) superlative hai aur Option (D) uncompared positive form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Irregular grading of much/many ➔ more ➔ most.
questions.hint: 'Evidence' uncountable noun hai, aur 'than' ke sath comparative form 'more' aayegi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correct word to complete the judicial instruction:
"Until ___ orders are passed by the Division Bench, the interim stay shall continue."

options.text: farther
further
farthest
furthermore

questions.explanation: 'Farther' strictly physical / geographical distance ke liye use hota hai (jaise: 'Jaipur is farther than Ajmer'). Jabki 'further' ka matlab 'additional', 'subsequent' ya 'more advanced in time/thought' hota hai. Yahan court ke 'additional / subsequent orders' ki baat ho rahi hai, isliye strictly 'further orders' aayega. Option (A) physical distance denote karta hai. Option (D) conjunctive adverb hai, determiner nahi.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Farther = physical distance; Further = additional / subsequent.
questions.hint: 'Additional' ya 'agle orders' ke context mein 'f-u-r-t-h-e-r' use hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the options below:

options.text: Ramesh is elder than his court assistant by four years.
Ramesh is older than his court assistant by four years.
Ramesh is elder from his court assistant by four years.
Ramesh is more older than his court assistant by four years.

questions.explanation: 'Elder' sirf ek hi family ke members (brothers, sisters, sons, daughters) ke liye noun se pehle attributively use hota hai ('my elder brother'). 'Elder' ke baad KABHI BHI 'than' nahi lagta. General age comparison (persons outside family ya things) ke liye conjunction 'than' ke sath strictly 'older than' use hota hai: 'Ramesh is older than his assistant'. Option (A) mein 'elder than' laga hai jo error hai. Option (C) preposition 'from' use karta hai. Option (D) double comparative hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Elder is confined to family relations and never takes 'than'. Use 'older than'.
questions.hint: 'Elder' ke baad kabhi 'than' nahi lagta. Non-family age comparison mein 'older than' use karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the following positive sentence of equality into an equivalent comparative sentence:
"Advocate Verma's memory is as sharp as Advocate Sharma's."

options.text: Advocate Sharma's memory is sharper than Advocate Verma's.
Advocate Sharma's memory is not sharper than Advocate Verma's.
Advocate Verma's memory is sharper than Advocate Sharma's.
Advocate Sharma's memory is the sharpest of all.

questions.explanation: Original sentence equality establish kar raha hai ('as sharp as'). Meaning preserve karne ke liye comparative sentence ko negative banana hoga: 'Advocate Sharma's memory is not sharper than Advocate Verma's' (Sharma ji ki memory Verma ji se zyada sharp nahi hai = dono barabar hain). Option (A) aur (C) ek ko doosre se superior bana dete hain. Option (D) superlative form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Equality 'as...as' transforms to negative comparative 'not + comparative + than'.
questions.hint: Dono barabar sharp hain. Transformed sentence ye assert karega ki ek doosre se zyada sharp NAHI hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the correct positive degree transformation of:
"Kolkata is larger than Jaipur."

options.text: Jaipur is not as large as Kolkata.
Kolkata is not as large as Jaipur.
Jaipur is as large as Kolkata.
No other city is as large as Kolkata.

questions.explanation: Original sentence kehta hai Kolkata Jaipur se bada hai (Kolkata > Jaipur). Positive degree mein convert karne par inferior entity 'Jaipur' subject banegi aur negative construction aayegi: 'Jaipur is not as large as Kolkata.' Option (B) Kolkata ko Jaipur se chhota bana deta hai (truth reversed). Option (C) dono ko equal bana deta hai. Option (D) 'No other city' universal scope bana deta hai jabki comparison sirf do cities ke beech tha.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Binary comparative ➔ Negative positive with transposed subjects.
questions.hint: 'Jaipur' ko start mein layein aur negative construction 'not as large as Kolkata' banayein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the superlative sentence into a comparative sentence:
"Gold is the most precious of all metals."

options.text: Gold is more precious than any metal.
Gold is more precious than any other metal.
Gold is more precious than most other metals.
Gold is as precious as any other metal.

questions.explanation: Gold unique apex metal hai ('the most precious'). Comparative transformation mein gold ko remaining metals se compare karne ke liye 'any other' lagana mandatory hai aur singular noun 'metal' aayega: 'Gold is more precious than any other metal.' Option (A) mein 'other' omitted hai jisse gold khud se compare hone lagta hai. Option (C) 'most other' subset group ('one of the') ke liye use hota hai. Option (D) positive equality form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05 & RC-06: The + Superlative ➔ Comparative + than ANY OTHER + Singular Noun.
questions.hint: 'More precious than' ke baad 'any other' aur singular noun 'metal' check karein.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the positive sentence into a superlative sentence:
"No other city in Rajasthan is as populated as Jaipur."

options.text: Jaipur is most populated city in Rajasthan.
Jaipur is the most populated city in Rajasthan.
Jaipur is one of the most populated cities in Rajasthan.
Jaipur is more populated than all cities in Rajasthan.

questions.explanation: 'No other city... is as populated as Jaipur' state karta hai ki Jaipur Rajasthan ki akeli sabse zyada populated city hai (unique apex). Superlative degree mein subject 'Jaipur' aayega, definite article 'the' aayega, aur 'most populated city in Rajasthan' banega: 'Jaipur is the most populated city in Rajasthan.' Option (A) mein mandatory article 'the' missing hai. Option (C) 'one of the' lagakar use subset group bana deta hai (meaning distortion). Option (D) comparative form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: NO OTHER + Singular Noun ➔ Subject + is + THE + Superlative + Singular Noun.
questions.hint: Unique number-1 city ke liye superlative mein 'the most populated' aayega ('one of the' nahi).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the comparative sentence into a positive sentence:
"The cheetah is faster than any other land animal."

options.text: No other land animal is as fast as the cheetah.
No other land animals are as fast as the cheetah.
Very few land animals are as fast as the cheetah.
Other land animals are not faster than the cheetah.

questions.explanation: Comparative formula 'faster than any other land animal' unique apex denote karta hai. Iska positive transformation 'NO OTHER + Singular Noun' se start hota hai: 'No other land animal is as fast as the cheetah.' Option (B) mein plural 'animals' aur plural verb 'are' laga hai jo standard rule ke against hai. Option (C) 'Very few' subset ranking ke liye hota hai. Option (D) non-standard negative phrasing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Comparative + than any other + Singular Noun ➔ NO OTHER + Singular Noun + is + as...as.
questions.hint: Sentence 'No other land animal' (singular noun + singular verb 'is') se start hona chahiye.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: Subset Group: 'One of the' to Comparative
questions.question:
Transform the superlative sentence into a comparative sentence:
"The High Court of Rajasthan is one of the oldest High Courts in India."

options.text: The High Court of Rajasthan is older than any other High Court in India.
The High Court of Rajasthan is older than most other High Courts in India.
The High Court of Rajasthan is older than most other High Court in India.
No other High Court in India is as old as the High Court of Rajasthan.

questions.explanation: Original sentence mein 'one of the oldest High Courts' hai, yaani Rajasthan High Court top bracket ke purane High Courts mein se ek hai (akela number-1 nahi hai). Iska comparative transformation 'than MOST OTHER + PLURAL NOUN' se hota hai: 'The High Court of Rajasthan is older than most other High Courts in India.' Option (A) 'any other' lagakar ise akela oldest bana deta hai (meaning distortion). Option (C) singular 'High Court' use karta hai jo 'most other' ke sath galat hai. Option (D) positive degree hai aur scope bhi distort karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: One of the + Superlative + Plural Noun ➔ Comparative + than MOST OTHER + Plural Noun.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ke comparative transformation mein 'any other' nahi, balki 'than most other + plural noun' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.subtopic: Subset Group: 'One of the' to Positive
questions.question:
Choose the correct positive transformation of:
"Rohan is one of the most competent system assistants in the department."

options.text: No other system assistant in the department is as competent as Rohan.
Very few system assistants in the department are as competent as Rohan.
Very few system assistant in the department is as competent as Rohan.
Rohan is as competent as any other system assistant in the department.

questions.explanation: 'One of the most competent' top-tier subset ko denote karta hai. Iska positive form 'VERY FEW + Plural Noun + Plural Verb' se banta hai: 'Very few system assistants in the department are as competent as Rohan.' Option (A) 'No other' unique apex bana deta hai (false equivalence). Option (C) singular noun 'assistant' aur singular verb 'is' use karta hai jo 'Very few' ke sath grammatically incorrect hai. Option (D) general parity assert kar raha hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: One of the ➔ VERY FEW + Plural Noun + Plural Verb + as...as.
questions.hint: 'One of the' ka positive transformation 'Very few' aur plural noun/verb ('assistants... are') se start hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Transform the positive sentence into a superlative sentence:
"Very few judgments of this court were as impactful as the 2024 verdict."

options.text: The 2024 verdict was the most impactful judgment of this court.
The 2024 verdict was one of the most impactful judgments of this court.
The 2024 verdict was one of the most impactful judgment of this court.
The 2024 verdict was more impactful than any other judgment of this court.

questions.explanation: Original sentence 'Very few judgments... were as impactful' state karta hai ki court ke bohot kam faisle is verdict jitne impactful the. Iska superlative transformation strictly 'one of the + most impactful + PLURAL NOUN' se hoga: 'The 2024 verdict was one of the most impactful judgments of this court.' Option (A) ise akela number-1 bana deta hai ('the most impactful judgment'). Option (C) singular 'judgment' use karta hai jo 'one of the' ke rule ke against hai. Option (D) comparative form hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: VERY FEW + Plural Noun ➔ Subject + was + ONE OF THE + Superlative + PLURAL NOUN.
questions.hint: 'Very few' ka superlative 'one of the most impactful judgments' (plural) hota hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Choose the grammatically correct sentence comparing exactly TWO entities:
"Of the two legal briefs submitted by counsel, ___."

options.text: the first one is the best
the first one is the better
the first one is better
the first one is most convincing

questions.explanation: English grammar ka fundamental rule hai: Jab total entities strictly DO hon ('Of the two legal briefs'), toh Superlative Degree ('the best', 'most convincing') use karna prohibited hai. Do entities ke beech comparative degree use hoti hai, aur selection hone ke karan comparative adjective se pehle definite article 'THE' lagta hai: 'the first one is THE BETTER'. Option (A) aur (D) superlative use kar rahe hain jo do entities ke case mein invalid hain. Option (C) mein required article 'the' missing hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: When comparing exactly two entities, use 'THE + Comparative' ('the better of the two').
questions.hint: Do cheezon mein superlative ('best') nahi lagta; 'the better' lagta hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Identify the grammatically correct parallel progression sentence:

options.text: The more you prepare for the High Court exam, better your marks will be.
The more you prepare for the High Court exam, the better your marks will be.
More you prepare for the High Court exam, the better your marks will be.
The more you prepare for the High Court exam, the best your marks will be.

questions.explanation: Parallel proportional increase ya decrease express karne ke liye dono clauses mein 'The + Comparative' ka hona mandatory hai: 'The more you prepare..., the better your marks will be.' Option (A) mein second clause se article 'the' missing hai. Option (C) mein first clause se 'the' missing hai. Option (D) superlative 'the best' use kar raha hai jo parallel progression mein invalid hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Parallel Progression: 'The + Comparative..., the + Comparative...'.
questions.hint: Dono clauses 'The + Comparative' se start hone chahiye ('The more..., the better...').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Choose the grammatically flawless sentence among the options:

options.text: For judicial assistants, accuracy is more preferable than speed.
For judicial assistants, accuracy is preferable than speed.
For judicial assistants, accuracy is preferable to speed.
For judicial assistants, accuracy is more preferable to speed.

questions.explanation: Adjective 'preferable' Latin comparative class ko belong karta hai. Iske do strict rules hain: (1) Iske sath conjunction 'than' nahi lagta, strictly preposition 'TO' lagta hai ('preferable to'); (2) Iske pehle comparative marker 'more' lagana completely prohibited hai kyunki 'preferable' already comparative force carry karta hai. Isliye strictly Option (C) 'preferable to speed' sahi hai. Option (A), (B) aur (D) in rules ko violate karte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: 'Preferable' takes 'TO' (never 'than', never 'more').
questions.hint: 'Preferable' ke sath 'to' lagta hai aur 'more' bilkul nahi lagta.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question:
Select the correct sentence comparing two qualities of the SAME individual:
"The junior clerk is ___ than ___."

options.text: wiser than intelligent
more wise than intelligent
wisest than intelligent
more wiser than intelligent

questions.explanation: English grammar rule: Jab hum do alag persons ko compare nahi kar rahe hote balki EK HI PERSON KI DO ALAG QUALITIES ka comparison karte hain, toh single-syllable adjective hone ke bawjood '-er' suffix use nahi ho sakta; strictly 'MORE + base adjective' use hota hai: 'The junior clerk is more wise than intelligent.' Option (A) '-er' suffix use karta hai jo do alag logon ke liye hota hai. Option (C) superlative hai. Option (D) double comparative error hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Single Entity Two Qualities ➔ Strictly 'MORE [Adj 1] than [Adj 2]'.
questions.hint: Ek hi person ki do qualities compare hone par single-syllable adjective mein bhi 'more wise' aayega, 'wiser' nahi.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Which of the following sentences correctly applies the rule of comparison?

options.text: London is more populated than any city in India.
London is more populated than any other city in India.
Mumbai is more populated than any city in India.
London is most populated than any city in India.

questions.explanation: Self-exclusion rule ke mutabiq, word 'other' tab lagta hai jab subject usi category/group ka member ho jisse wo compare ho raha hai (jaise: 'Mumbai is more populated than any OTHER city in India'). Lekin London India ki city nahi hai (external comparison), isliye London ko Indian cities ke set se exclude karne ke liye 'other' lagane ki zaroorat nahi hai: 'London is more populated than any city in India' bilkul correct hai. Option (B) galat tarike se London ko Indian city assume kar leta hai. Option (C) mein Mumbai ke liye 'other' missing hai. Option (D) comparative structure mein 'most' use karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Do NOT use 'other' when comparing a subject with a group to which it does NOT belong.
questions.hint: London Indian city nahi hai, isliye yahan 'other' lagane ki zaroorat nahi hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09

questions.question: Find the grammatically INCORRECT sentence among the following options:

options.text: This judicial dictionary is preferable to the older edition.
Platinum is heavier than all other metals in this collection.
Of the two advocates arguing the bail plea, Mr. Roy is the most articulate.
The higher the bench sits, the greater the legal authority it commands.

questions.explanation: Option (C) grammatically incorrect hai kyunki sentence specify kar raha hai 'Of the two advocates' (strictly DO advocates). Do entities ke beech comparison mein Superlative Degree ('the most articulate') lagana strict error hai. Correct sentence hona chahiye: '...Mr. Roy is the MORE articulate.' Option (A) 'preferable to' flawlessly follow karta hai. Option (B) 'than all other + plural noun' correctly follow karta hai. Option (D) 'The + Comparative..., the + Comparative...' parallel progression perfectly follow karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: When comparing two entities, superlative degree cannot be used; use 'the + comparative'.
questions.hint: 'Of the two advocates' mein do log hain, isliye 'the most articulate' galat hai.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L09
